admission.justification: The rejected aggregate/exception design and chosen per-tool/reference design constrain every later owner that rewrites or adds a tool description.

alternatives.option: Use a 600-character ordinary per-tool ceiling and move longer calling/reference material to an openable skill or reference, preserving only explicit later-owner transition pins.
alternatives.reason: Every owning change can meet its own final bound without requiring an aggregate last leaf, and calling detail remains reachable without retransmitting it in every tool advertisement.

alternatives.option: Use an aggregate description budget or a permanent exception table for selected large descriptions.
alternatives.reason: An aggregate is landing-order dependent, and permanent exceptions retain the repeated reference-material cost; the developer required the 600-character bound without such a table.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The developer changes the context-cost tradeoff or an evidenced ordinary tool cannot retain usable calling guidance with its pointer under the chosen ceiling.

consequences: Later description owners must maintain the pointer, ordinary character bounds and exact transition pins; argument descriptions cannot become a substitute storage location for long reference material.
context: Repeated tool descriptions carried full calling/reference material. The task considered aggregate and exception bounds before the developer chose an ordinary per-tool ceiling and an openable longer explanation.
decider: Developer D126 as recorded in the canonical MIK-R112@v1 packet and leaf decision log; D128 preserves dispatch_agent until its replacement lands.
